title: Seeing Through VisualBERT: A Causal Adventure on Memetic Landscapes
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the causal interpretability of multimodal models in detecting offensive memes. Specifically, it measured whether the models base their offensiveness predictions on correct causal concepts (such as 'anti-muslim' or specific references to Jews) or if they rely on spurious correlations and dataset-wide biases when processing religious terms and imagery.
findings: The models exhibited strong dataset-wide biases regarding religious terms. The evaluation showed that the mere presence of the word 'Mohammed' could lead the model to classify a meme as offensive and incorrectly attribute it to 'anti-muslim' keywords. Similarly, the word 'jew' prompted the model to associate memes with concepts like 'violence' and 'genocide' regardless of context. This highlights the impact of dataset bias, as about 39.3% of the training dataset consisted of religious memes.
